phase1.explanation:
Variables are labeled boxes — you already knew that from the moment I said it, but let's actually open a few.

Java has eight [[term:primitive]] types built in, but we only need four to get moving: [[term:int]] for whole numbers, [[term:double]] for anything with a decimal, [[term:char]] for a single character (always single quotes, `'A'`, never double), and [[term:boolean]] for true/false.

Declaring one always follows the same shape: `type name = value;` — the box's label (its type) comes first, then its name, then what's actually inside it.

[[key:Naming a variable has real rules, not just style preferences]]: it can start with a letter, an underscore, or a dollar sign, never a digit, and it can't be one of Java's reserved words like `int` or `class`. Convention-wise, we write variable names in [[term:camelCase]] — `myVariableName`, not `my_variable_name` or `MyVariableName`.

One more thing worth locking in now: `System.out.println` will happily glue a String and a variable together with `+` — that's how `"Age: " + age` turns into readable output instead of two separate things sitting next to each other.
phase1.openingDialogue: Variables are like labeled boxes — you put values in them and give them names! 📦

phase2.errorMessage:
DataTypesExample.java:5: error: incompatible types: String cannot be converted to char
        char grade = "A";
                     ^
1 error
phase2.explanation:
[[warn:char uses single quotes, always]] — `'A'`, not `"A"`. Double quotes build a String, and Java is strongly typed enough to refuse handing a String where a char belongs, even one that's a single letter.

The compiler actually spells this out almost word for word: "incompatible types: String cannot be converted to char." [[key:That error message alone tells you exactly what's wrong and where]] — get comfortable reading these, because Java's compiler errors are usually more helpful than people expect.

phase3.openingDialogue: Alright, show me you can handle these variables~ 🎯

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a program with variables for:
• A student's age (int) — set to 20
• Their GPA (double) — set to 3.75
• Their first initial (char) — set to 'J'
• Whether they're enrolled (boolean) — set to true

Print all 4 values with descriptive labels.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:Fun fact]]: a Java char isn't just one byte like in some older languages — it's a 16-bit UTF-16 code unit, which is part of why Java could represent a huge range of world languages and symbols from day one, not just the basic English alphabet.
phase5.openingDialogue: One more thing before you go~
